2.text: of various pendants and tassels made of skin

3.text: and beads, and fastened to various parts of

4.text: the body or dress, often also made into rings,

5.text: bracelets, and necklaces to be worn for per-

6.text: sonal adornment.¹ In addition to these, I

7.text: will mention the round patches of skin, often

8.text: with a tassel in the centre (Fig. 292), which

9.text: are considered as highly effective amulets

10.text: among the Chukchee,² the Pacific Koryak,

11.text: and the Asiatic Eskimo. They are sewed to

12.text: the coat, on the breast or on the shoulders,

13.text: and, if possible, against that part of the body

14.text: where the pain is felt, or at least is sup-

15.text: posed to be; for example, against the top of

16.text: the stomach in all internal sufferings, against

17.text: the shoulderblade in rheumatic affections of

18.text: the back, etc. A rough image of the “guar-

19.text: dian” is fastened in the centre. Often,

20.text: however, the figure takes an ornamental

21.text: character, and the “guardian” is replaced by

22.text: a woman’s figure, by a man dancing, or by a

23.text: warrior clad in Chukchee armor, all of which,

24.text: of course, may not be considered as images of

25.text: “spirits.” The whole object serves both magic

26.text: and ornamental purposes, as is the case with many other pendanst and tassels.
26.note: 'pendanst' is the book's own printer's error (transposed letters, expected 'pendants'); keyed as printed per keying_spec.md §2.14: "A printer's error is keyed as printed, and gt/ocr never repairs the book."
